Single-target consolidations to "rex-prd-engine" are non-deterministic until it is a stable anchor. - "packages/hench/src/prd/llm-gateway.ts" is imported from 3 zones (tests-hench, tests-hench-integration, tests-hench-unit) — a cross-cutting dependency every one of them is coupled to [warning] (hench)
- ... and 24 more

### Patterns

- info: migrations/registry.ts is a clean extension seam. Its header says one entry per migration folder and nothing reads it except the migrate command, so adding or removing a migration touches one file. [info] (rex)
- info: migration-plan-data.ts says it is pure and deterministic, keyed by v1 item id, and never shells out. Outside facts are injected by the caller. This keeps the migration plan replayable, so new code in this folder should keep that boundary. [info] (rex)
- info: escalate.ts centralises retry/escalation for validated LLM calls. New LLM-calling analyze modules (decompose, consolidation-guard, *-reason) should go through it rather than adding their own retry loops. [warning] (rex-cli)
- warning: hub/exec-gateway.ts is a web gateway onto @n-dx/llm-client that is missing from the gateway table in CLAUDE.md/docs/architecture/gateways.md. Register it, and confirm it is web's only llm-client import surface, to satisfy the one-gateway-per-source-package rule. [warning] (web-server)
- info: The hub keeps project servers unchanged by running each as a child `web serve` on a loopback port, with per-project ndxBin. Because of that isolation, single-project assumptions in src/server/ do not need hub awareness, and the proxy/base-path stripping is the only contract between the two. [info] (web-server)
- info: api.ts (inbound) and external.ts (outbound) form a clear two-sided boundary for the viewer. The cycles show that api.ts is also imported from inside the viewer, so restrict it to sibling-zone consumers as its header describes. [warning] (web-viewer)

### Relationships

- Tightly coupled modules: packages/hench/src/agent/lifecycle/shared.ts and packages/hench/src/types/output.ts — 141 cross-file calls (unidirectional). Consider extracting shared interface or merging [info]
- info: The single rex-cli → rex-fix edge is most likely the CLI dispatcher loading commands/fix.ts. That is a normal command registration, not a layering violation. Treat the fix/ → core/parent-completion.ts coupling described in fix/index.ts as the boundary that matters. [info] (rex-fix)
